item.title: Gilead Hepatitis D Drug Approval
item.description:
• Summary: The U.S. FDA approved Gilead Sciences' hepatitis D drug bulevirtide (brand name Hepcludex), four years after an initial rejection. Bulevirtide is a first-in-class entry inhibitor that blocks the sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP) receptor, preventing the hepatitis D virus from infecting hepatocytes. The approval provides the first FDA-endorsed therapy for hepatitis D, a severe form of viral hepatitis that affects patients co-infected with hepatitis B.
  • MoAs: NTCP-mediated entry inhibitor
  • Sources: Endpoints News

item.title: Moderna mRNA Flu Shot
item.description:
• Summary: Moderna's mRNA-based influenza vaccine, which was previously rebuffed by regulators, is set to face scrutiny from an FDA advisory committee (AdComm). The committee will review data to determine the vaccine's safety and efficacy.
  • MoAs: mRNA vaccine encoding influenza virus antigens to induce an immune response against seasonal flu strains.
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.title: ECDC STI Report
item.description:
• Summary: According to an ECDC report covered by Pharmaceutical Technology, sexually transmitted infection (STI) cases across Europe have reached record highs, raising implications for public health and pharmaceutical interventions.
